title.value: Endorsing Complexity Through Diversity: Computational Psychiatry Meets Big Data Analytics
title.justification: The title is explicitly stated at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: Endorsing Complexity Through Diversity: Computational Psychiatry Meets Big Data Analytics

extractions.description: The paper discusses how large datasets and big data analytics can transform the field of psychiatry, particularly in understanding and diagnosing psychiatric disorders. It highlights the use of diverse data sources, such as genomics and imaging, to improve diagnosis and treatment by considering population diversity in psychiatric research. The paper stresses the importance of complex data analyses using computational methods to reveal insights into psychiatric disorders, although it acknowledges the trade-off between model complexity and interpretability.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily discusses advancements in computational methods and big data analytics in the field of psychiatry, focusing on diagnosis and treatment of psychiatric disorders, without addressing Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development directly.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Sharpening diagnosis and optimizing treatment choice are key challenges that psychiatry is facing. Since mental health cannot be measured the same way diabetes can be assessed through plasma levels of insulin or glucose, the diagnostic system is unstable.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not directly address any aspect of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development. Its focus is on psychiatry and big data analytics, which do not fit into the provided categories related to sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: Therefore, expanding data resources was a prerequisite to estimating the flexible, highly adaptive models with a large capacity to represent convoluted relationships between variables, such as hierarchical dependencies and higher-order nonlinearity.

primary_sub_category.quote: For example, linear regression–type models are potentially the most amenable to human interpretation, whereas deep learning techniques are struggling to offer human-readable interpretations of what is going on in their visceral internals.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on computational methods and big data analytics in psychiatry, which is not covered by the existing Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development categories.
new_primary_category.quote: The recent advent of population datasets challenges the way we are used to quantitatively analyzing and drawing insights about psychiatric disorders, including autism spectrum disorder or schizophrenia.
